one_line: Better Stack beginner walkthrough of GSAP after Webflow made GSAP and its plugins free: tweens, stagger, timelines, paused playback and ScrollTrigger scrubbing a video. No benchmarks; the main news is the pricing change.
summary: The presenter announces that Webflow has made GSAP and its plugins completely free, which he presents as removing the one drawback of the library. He opens with demos of GSAP-built sites (scroll animation, a portfolio using Observer and Motion Path, SVG morphing with text on a motion path) to show its range. The core lesson covers four tween types (to, from, fromTo, set), animating arbitrary properties including custom numeric properties on plain objects, and repeat/yoyo. He then shows stagger for sequencing elements by DOM order, and gsap.timeline() with position offsets for finer control. Playback control comes next: start paused, call play(), and restart when progress completes. The last section uses ScrollTrigger with scrub to tie a video's currentTime to scroll position, which he says resembles the GTA 6 landing page effect. He says he would not ship his primitive version to production.
speakers: Unnamed Better Stack host (not named in transcript)

key_ideas.idea: GSAP and its plugins are now free; the speaker credits Webflow with making the change.
key_ideas.detail: Presented as removing the paid-plugin barrier. Stated claim only, no license terms given in the video.

key_ideas.idea: Every GSAP animation is a tween, and there are four kinds: to, from, fromTo and set.
key_ideas.detail: to animates from the current state to given values; from animates from given values to the current state; fromTo specifies both ends; set applies the values instantly. Selectors can be a class name, an ID or the element object.

key_ideas.idea: Tweens can animate essentially any numeric property, including custom properties on a plain JavaScript object.
key_ideas.detail: Demo tweens an object's count key from 1 to 10 and logs it with an onUpdate callback, so GSAP is usable as a generic number-interpolation engine.

key_ideas.idea: repeat: -1 loops forever and yoyo reverses direction instead of restarting.
key_ideas.detail: Shows looping behavior as built-in tween options rather than hand-written loops.

key_ideas.idea: stagger offsets each element's start by its order in the matched set, which is the simple way to sequence several elements.
key_ideas.detail: Same-class elements start together by default. stagger set to a time value starts each one that much later. Stagger is limited to a fixed interval per element, so custom sequencing needs a timeline.

key_ideas.idea: Timelines give explicit control over sequencing. Tweens are added with timeline.to instead of gsap.to, and each has a position parameter.
key_ideas.detail: Position can be an absolute time in seconds, an offset from the end of the timeline, or a negative offset that overlaps the previous tween. The timeline grows as tweens are added. Unlike stagger, tweens can have different durations.

key_ideas.idea: Playback is controllable: create the timeline with paused set to true, call play() from a button, and restart the animation once its progress is complete.
key_ideas.detail: Shows the timeline as a programmable object rather than a fire-and-forget animation.

key_ideas.idea: ScrollTrigger with scrub: true ties an animation's progress to scroll position, so the video's currentTime tween plays forward when scrolling down and in reverse when scrolling up.
key_ideas.detail: The effect is a video animated from currentTime 0 to its duration, not a set of rendered images. The speaker believes the GTA 6 site uses a canvas-based approach with GSAP, and says he would not ship his primitive version to production.

techniques.name: Basic tween on a selector
techniques.how: Call gsap.to with a target (class name, ID or element) and an object of properties to animate. The demo translates a circle by 40px and changes its fill to blue; the narration does not state the exact property key used for the translation.
techniques.when: Any simple one-off DOM animation where you want the browser to animate from current state to a target.

techniques.name: from / fromTo / set variants
techniques.how: Use gsap.from to animate in from specified values, gsap.fromTo to specify both start and end, and gsap.set to apply values instantly with no animation.
techniques.when: Entrance animations (from), exact start and end control (fromTo), and initial state setup (set).

techniques.name: Animate a custom object property
techniques.how: Create a plain object such as {count: 1}, tween its count property to 10, and read it in an onUpdate callback to log or render each intermediate value.
techniques.when: Counters, number displays, or driving any non-DOM value through GSAP's easing and timing.

techniques.name: Looping with repeat and yoyo
techniques.how: Set repeat to -1 for an infinite loop. Set yoyo to true to reverse direction on each repeat instead of jumping back to the start.
techniques.when: Ambient or idle motion such as pulsing or bobbing elements.

techniques.name: Stagger for ordered starts
techniques.how: Add a stagger property to a tween applied to a class and set its value in seconds. Elements start in DOM order, each delayed by the stagger value. The demo uses 0.5 seconds.
techniques.when: A list or grid of same-type elements animating one after another with equal delays and equal durations.

techniques.name: Timeline with position parameter
techniques.how: Create with gsap.timeline(), add tweens with timeline.to(...), and pass a position value after the tween's vars and a comma. Use an absolute time in seconds to start at a fixed point, a positive value for a gap after the timeline's current end, or a negative value to overlap the previous tween.
techniques.when: Sequences with different durations, overlapping animations, or any choreography stagger cannot express.

techniques.name: Paused timeline with manual play
techniques.how: Create the timeline with paused set to true, call play() from a click handler, and restart it when its progress has reached the end.
techniques.when: Animations triggered by user action rather than page load, or re-runnable demos.

techniques.name: Scroll-scrubbed video
techniques.how: Register the ScrollTrigger plugin. Get the video element by its ID, tween its currentTime from 0 to its duration, and set scrub: true in the ScrollTrigger config. The speaker wraps the video in a container div named scroll content. The narration does not show the exact ID or the plugin registration call.
techniques.when: Scroll-linked video effects where the frames should follow scroll position in both directions. The speaker does not recommend this exact setup for production.

tools: Webflow (named as the company that made GSAP free, not a tool used in the demos)

numbers.claim: Pricing: GSAP and its plugins are now free (no dollar figure given).
Demo tween translates an element 40px and changes its fill to blue.
Demo counter animates a custom property from 1 to 10.
Demo stagger: three boxes each translated 500px with duration 3, then a 0.5s stagger example.
Timeline demo: green tween lasts 2s; purple tween position set to 1s, so it starts while green is still running and both end together.

hot_takes: The main news is the pricing change. The rest is a beginner-level API walkthrough with no benchmarks, comparisons or production advice.
The speaker says he would not ship his video-scrub recreation to production. He believes the GTA 6 site uses canvas with GSAP. He states this as a belief, not as checked fact.
The title's 100% free claim is the speaker's report of Webflow's decision. The transcript includes no license text or source.

relevance.why: Browser animation library tutorial; no link to AgentOS infra, inference, memory or observability.
No overlap with checkpointing, Claude Code CLI harnessing, plan/critique loops or approvals.
